# AGENT-ENV — the machine-checked repo operating contract

You are working in a large monorepo. The facts below are the ones that cost a
fresh agent a failed command or a wrong edit when undiscovered. They are
GENERATED from the real config (package.json, the vite config, the on-disk
layout), so they cannot drift out of sync the way a hand-written note does.

- **Repo root:** `@papercupai/papercusp-monorepo`
- **Package manager:** `npm@11.19.0`

## Where shared code lives

There is **no single shared-code directory** — `libs/` and `packages/` both
exist and are both npm workspaces, with shared packages split across them under no
stated rule (e.g. `test-config` lives in `libs/`, not `packages/`). Guessing the
wrong root is a `No such file or directory`. Search across them before assuming:

```
ls -d libs/*<name>* packages/*<name>* 2>/dev/null   # find which root actually holds it
```

Applications live separately under `apps/` (each is its own workspace).

## Running tests

`vitest` is **hoisted to the repo root**, and MOST packages have no local copy —
so a package-local invocation is exit-127 DOA. (A few packages that pin a different
vitest major do ship their own; the root binary is the safe default everywhere else.)

```
node_modules/.bin/vitest            # EXISTS (the hoisted binary — the safe default)
packages/agent-mcp/node_modules/.bin/vitest   # does NOT exist → a package-local call there is exit-127 DOA
```

Run a suite one of these ways (both resolve the hoisted binary):

```
npm run test:file -- <path>                       # the supported wrapper
node_modules/.bin/vitest run <path>               # the hoisted binary directly
scripts/pc-heavy.sh node_modules/.bin/vitest run <path>   # REQUIRED for heavy runs on the shared box
```

On the shared 128-core box, heavy commands (a full suite, a build) must go
through `scripts/pc-heavy.sh` (nice + a flock concurrency semaphore) or the
admission guard rejects them under load.

Some apps need their own vitest config, e.g. `apps/operator`:

```
node_modules/.bin/vitest run <path> --config apps/operator/vitest.config.ts
```

## Cross-tree alias trap (operator-vite)

In `apps/operator-vite/vite.config.ts`, the `@` alias resolves to `../operator`
relative to that config — i.e. it points at a **DIFFERENT app** (`apps/operator`,
the Next tree), not into operator-vite itself. So inside `apps/operator-vite`, an
intuitive `@/…` import silently crosses into another app's source tree.
**Intra-app imports here must be relative.** Nothing at the import site warns you.

## Desktop (Tauri)

The Tauri webview serves a **prebuilt, hashed bundle**, not the dev server — so
source edits appear to do nothing until you rebuild the bundle. If a UI change
is not showing up, rebuild before assuming the edit was wrong.
